The displayed six-monomial generator and stationary moment identities yield the rational unilateral transform; this is symbolically reconstructed by the embedded checker. Decomposition as a positive fourfold convolution times H+B R(t), with H>0, reduces signs to a strictly increasing ratio R(t). Log-concavity of convolutions of one-sided exponentials proves strict increase, and the slowest exponential rate gives its exact limit. This derives the closed dimension-dependent threshold and one and only one simple crossing when supercritical; equality gives finite-lag positivity. The verifier additionally reproduces the resolvent identities and 12 independent matrix-exponential checks. No infinite claim relies on those finite checks.

value.rationale: The observable compares two time orderings of the same fourth-degree joint moment, so it captures dynamic information inaccessible to the stationary fourth moment and two-time covariance alone. A sharp dimension-five onset, a nontrivial high-dimensional radical threshold, and a unique oriented sign reversal establish a structural phase boundary across every positive model parameter, rather than an arbitrary finite-parameter calculation. The result is motivated by exact active-matter oscillator models and potential higher-order diagnostics of temporal dynamics, without claiming direct entropy production or an experimental error bound.
